title: Testing the price already covers

company.company_business: IT implementation and managed services for mid-size Indian businesses

narrative_template:
{customer} asked for a second round of user-acceptance testing on its fixed-price project. The contract price covers up to three rounds. The testing took ₹4,00,000 of Kalmira's staff time. How does this cost affect the cost-to-cost measure of progress?

Round amounts to the nearest rupee and percentages to one decimal place. All names are fictional.

rubric.text: Testing within the contract counts in costs to date.

check.correct: Include it in costs to date

options: Include it in costs to date
Leave it out of the measure of progress
explanation: Costs of work the contract pays for depict progress and stay in the measure. B19 excludes only costs that do not reflect performance.

mistakes.choice: Leave it out of the measure of progress
mistakes.feedback: This testing is part of the work the price pays for, and it moves the project towards completion, so it counts in costs to date. Only costs that do not depict progress, such as wasted effort, are left out (B19(a)).
